subject: Re: Renewal: EmberCloud 2029 capacity + pricing discussion
messages:
From: Susan Park <susan.park@embercloud.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Nov 2028 15:23:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal planning + capacity uplift

Marissa —

Thanks for the chat last week. EmberCloud's usage spiked significantly in Q3 and we're forecasting continued growth into 2029. We want to lock a renewal for January but have a few asks up-front:

- Can Redwood hold current rates for a 12-month window if we commit to a 30% increase in reserved capacity?
- If we do a staged commit (30% year 1, 50% year 2), what credits do you offer for overage during the first 90 days?
- We have production latency SLAs for a subset of traffic — will a price hold extend to Dedicated capacity or only Shared?

I copied our platform ops and legal (Amir) — they'd like a proposed structure and any amendment text you can share before our procurement cycle starts.

Best,
Susan Park
Head of Platform, EmberCloud
ops@embercloud.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Susan Park <susan.park@embercloud.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + capacity uplift

Susan —

Really appreciate the forward signal. We can put together a clean set of options; quick summary below and I'll attach a model you can drill into. See EmberCloud_MA_Pricing_Model.xlsx attached.

Option A — 12m Price Hold (fast-track)- Requirement: 30% committed uplift on reserved tokens/embeddings for 12 months- Benefit: current per-token rates held; overages billed at discounted incremental rate (15% off list)- Credit: 1% of committed value credited monthly for first 3 months to offset ramp spikes

Option B — Staged Commit + Staggered Credits- Year 1: 30% uplift (price hold)- Year 2: 50% uplift (new baseline)- Benefit: phased true-up; overages in ramp months 1–3 receive a blended credit (see sheet "Ramp Credits")

Option C — Dedicated SLA + Price Guard (for latency-critical traffic)- Requirement: map latency-critical routes to Dedicated pool- Benefit: price hold can be extended to Dedicated instances if commit and term (24 months) agreed; also offers higher SLA with uptime credit band

Next steps:
1) Suggest a 30-minute call next week to lock which option you prefer.
2) If you lean C we’ll need capacity mapping from your ops team (Karthik can run the mapping).
3) I’m sending a draft amendment (redwood_proposed-amendment_v3.pdf) internally and to legal for a narrow price-hold clause you can review.

If that looks sane I’ll loop Laura for renewal approval and get our legal team to prepare a DocuSign.

—
Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Susan Park <susan.park@embercloud.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Nov 2028 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + capacity uplift

Susan — quick add from my side:

We can tier the discount to make the economics linear:
- 30% uplift -> additional 10% effective discount on committed units
- 40–49% uplift -> 12.5% discount
- 50%+ uplift -> 15% discount + 60-day burst buffer included

I've highlighted the tier math in the attached spreadsheet. Happy to walk through on the call.

Cheers,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Susan Park <susan.park@embercloud.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Amir Khan <amir.khan@embercloud.com>, ops@embercloud.com
Date: Tue, 5 Dec 2028 08:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + capacity uplift

Thanks Marissa and Ben — this is helpful. A couple clarifying points before we pick a path:

1) SLA scope: we operate two traffic classes. For class A (latency < 100ms) we need dedicated guarantees. Can the price-hold in Option C explicitly reference those routes and the dedicated pool?
2) Legal will want the price-hold clause to include a defined mechanism for true-ups and a credit ladder for repeated shortfall months (we can draft language).
3) Procurement prefers a 12-month effective price hold with an option to extend if year-over-year usage exceeds 40%.

Can Karthik map our current class A flows to the Dedicated pool and estimate the upfront reserved capacity needed? Once we have that, Amit (Amir?) and I can align procurement schedule.

—
Susan
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Susan Park <susan.park@embercloud.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Dec 2028 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + capacity uplift

Susan —

Happy to run the mapping. A few notes up-front:
- If Class A traffic is isolated to Dedicated instances we can reserve a small hot pool (10–15% of peak) and attach a burst buffer for 60 days while you ramp.
- I recommend a partitioned Dedicated pool by route group so we can apply tighter KV cache and batching controls to keep latency consistent.
- I'll attach a simple capacity diagram (capacity-mapping-diagram.png) showing the mapping and recommended headroom.

I can run this mapping with access to your last 90 days of route-level token counts and p95 latency slices; if you can share a CSV of that export Ops, I’ll have a first cut by Wednesday.

—
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Dec 2028 11:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + capacity uplift

Team —

This looks like a good path forward. Quick internal plan:
1) Marissa/Bob (sic: Ben) finalize the preferred commercial option with EmberCloud (likely Option C with a 12m price hold + 24m Dedicated extension clause).
2) Ben to confirm the exact uplift % we’ll sign to (we should be comfortable with a 30–50% band).
3) Karthik to deliver capacity mapping doc and the route CSV to include in the amendment.
4) I’ll kick legal to accept the narrow price-hold wording and prepare the amendment for signatures once we have the mapping.

Marissa — please send me the version of redwood_proposed-amendment_v3.pdf with your changes tracked. I’ll greenlight signature routing and request a DocuSign envelope.

—
Laura Bennett
